question: Can one curved log-flow term improve full-cohort pooled prediction over separate Round2 models?
flow: U_m=100*((Uf_cm_s/100)^4+(9.80665*g_fraction*3.5*d_mm/2000)^2)^(1/4); assumed P/P0=1, kappa=3.5, not row measurements
constraint: mixed_concave coefficient on negative squared log flow >=0; other coefficients unconstrained. No fixed peak and no planetary ranking.
fit: weighted log-rate ridge alpha1; groups weighted equally and weights normalized to row mean1. Training-only weighted standardization. Unpenalized weighted log intercept. No tuning, clipping, smearing or new labels.
splits: Reuse the corresponding frozen Round3 splits exactly:30 pooled,25 strict,1 Earth-only transfer
primary_gate: Full pooled ISS group MAE <=90% of separate Round2 0.010490585024313702, AND pooled Earth MAE <= separate Round2 0.013327813827982137. A 10% gain is a development screen, not a practical safety tolerance.
secondary_transfer_gate: MAE <=80% of nearest0.01662348484848485. No transfer tuning on ISS outcomes.
strict: Exclude U01 from both training and evaluation; 23 flight rows are9.5/12.7mm,11 excluded are6.4mm. Sensitivity cannot replace full-cohort result.
verification: GPU float64 fits; independently solve augmented least squares on CPU, verify constraints/KKT, predictions, grouped scores, exact control reproduction and preserved hashes
reporting: All models and failures, coverage, worst cases, descriptive paired group-bootstrap differences, fitted peak at19% O2. Peak is not lunar evidence. Reused development folds, no independent confirmation or deployment promotion.
execution: Blackwell CUDA required, no CPU fitting fallback. CPU preprocessing and independent verification. Freeze before fit; refuse overwrite.
